alternatives.root_cause: A bad checkout build was rolled out and fails on every order request.
alternatives.why_not: A crash-looping or unstartable artifact would usually show checkout itself unreachable and produce connection-level errors in frontend; a running service returning errors fits a wrong config value more cleanly, though only the change log would separate them.

alternatives.root_cause: payment (or another checkout-only dependency) became slow, and checkout's deadlines expired, turning latency into errors.
alternatives.why_not: The downstream services raised no alerts of their own, and the upstream symptom is error rate rather than the latency alerts a slow dependency usually trips first.

verdict.summary: checkout is failing all orders because one of its exclusive downstream endpoints (most likely payment) is configured with a wrong/unreachable address, so calls fail immediately at checkout and the error surfaces up through frontend and frontend-proxy to the load-generator.
verdict.reasoning: The alerting set is exactly checkout plus everything upstream of it (frontend -> frontend-proxy -> load-generator); no shared dependency alerts. If product-catalog or cart were broken, frontend and recommendation would show errors on their own paths, not only via checkout. That localises the fault to checkout itself or to a dependency only checkout uses (currency, email, payment, shipping). Those downstreams are silent, which fits a caller-side failure: checkout never reaches them, or reaches the wrong place, so they log nothing and raise no alert. The symptom is a high error rate rather than latency, so the calls are failing fast rather than hanging - that argues for a wrong address/port/credential in checkout's dependency configuration rather than a slow or frozen dependency.
open_questions: checkout's error text on failed orders - connection refused / DNS failure vs. an application-level error returned by payment
Whether payment, shipping, currency or email saw any request volume at all during the window
checkout's effective env/config for the payment and shipping endpoints versus the last known-good values
Whether checkout latency rose (dependency slow) or stayed flat (fail fast)
flagd flag state at onset, even though checkout is not shown as a flagd client
